name: Moldavite: Notes & Ideas
subtitle: Write, journal, connect
promotionalText: A simple place to write and organize your notes.
description: Moldavite is a simple notes app for iPhone and iPad. Write down thoughts, organize your notes, and find them when you need them. Your notes stay in your own Markdown files, with no account required.
whatsNew: Autumn is here. A new Autumn theme in light and dark, with a warm wheat page and maple accents. The home screen gets a little autumn field with a scarecrow, pumpkins and a leaf pile, plus leaves drifting down and a small pumpkin in Settings. Every theme now has a faint sun or moon in the corner and sparkling constellations. Turn the seasonal touches off in Settings › Layout › Seasonal touches. Lists in your notes are now saved the standard Markdown way, so they look right in other apps too.
notes:
Purpose and audience
Moldavite is a free Markdown notes app for iPhone and iPad for capturing ideas, writing daily notes and organizing your own writing. Notes are files in a workspace called a Forge. Local note-taking works without an account or internet connection.

Setup and main features
1. Launch Moldavite and complete the introductory screens. The Default Forge is created in local storage. No registration, login, payment or download is required.
2. Open Index in the left rail. In Notes, tap New, enter a title such as "Review note" and create it. Type a paragraph; edits save automatically. Close and reopen the note to check the saved text.
3. Use the editor's formatting controls for headings and lists. Index browses notes, folders and tags; Search (magnifying glass in the rail) finds notes by title or text.
4. Agenda opens daily notes. Links between notes are written as [[Review note]] and explored in Graph.
5. Optional note locking is in note actions. Lock a note with a test passphrase and enter it to unlock. The developer cannot recover a forgotten passphrase.
6. Optional iCloud: with iCloud Drive on, open Settings > General and turn on Use synced Forge. This opens a separate Forge shared across devices on the same Apple Account; local notes are not moved. No reviewer Apple Account credentials are needed.
7. Optional calendars: in Settings > Calendar, Apple Calendar asks for the system permission (choose Allow Full Access) and shows the device's events in Agenda. Google Calendar opens Apple's sign-in sheet for the user's own Google account with read-only access; Google shows an unverified-app notice while its review of the app is pending. Both only read events and are not needed to use the app.

Accounts, content and payments
There are no Moldavite accounts, registration or deletion flows, subscriptions, in-app purchases or paid features. Notes are private user content. There is no public feed, directory, messaging or publishing to other users, so reporting and blocking do not apply.

Services and implementation
Editing, storage and search run on the device: a React/TypeScript editor in WKWebView through Tauri, a Rust backend and SQLite. Optional external services are iCloud Drive for sync and, for calendar display only, Apple's EventKit and the Google Calendar API. Google sign-in uses ASWebAuthenticationSession with OAuth; the token stays in the device Keychain and calendar data goes only between the device and Google, never to the developer. There is no developer backend, advertising, analytics, payments or AI service. The iOS app has no desktop plugins, MCP, WordPress publishing or self-updates. Settings links to support and the privacy policy.

Regions
The same features are offered in every enabled storefront, subject to iCloud availability. France is excluded while ANSSI processes its encryption declaration; it has not been enabled.

Regulated services and third-party material
Moldavite is a general-purpose notes app, not a regulated financial, medical, gambling or similar service, and distributes no third-party content catalog. Dependencies and assets are used under their licenses. Note locking uses AES-256-GCM with Argon2id; the submission declares encryption implemented outside Apple's OS.
